headline: UK inflation rises to 3.6% in October, its highest in a year
summary: Consumer prices in the UK rose 3.6% in the 12 months to October, up from 3.5% in September, the Office for National Statistics said on 18 November. It is the fourth rise in a row.
why: Inflation stays well above the Bank of England’s 2% target, which matters for interest rates, mortgages and savings.

event.t: Core inflation, which leaves out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, stayed at 2.8%.
The ONS said fuel prices were again a major reason for the rise. Motor fuel cost 33.2% more than a year earlier, and a tobacco duty rise on 1 October also pushed prices up.
Food inflation slowed to 0.8% from 1.2% in September.

watch: The Bank of England’s next rate decision
